clue.text: Prohibition very strong in N.America

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud or strong playing

explanation.surface: A remark that temperance laws were especially severe in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prohibition' points at the American dry era, but here it is simply BAN. The definition is a placename pointer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a resort town in the Rocky Mountains of Alberta, Canada.

clue.text: Job, for example, for a turf accountant

definitions.text: Job, for example, for a turf accountant

parts.words: Job, for example, for a turf accountant
parts.note: Job is a book of the Bible, so its author made a book; a turf accountant is a racecourse bookie

explanation.walkthrough: A turf accountant is a British euphemism for a betting agent; Job reads as a job of work but is a biblical book.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting-shop proprietor takes wagers on races, and making a book is the trade term for taking bets.

clue.text: Bottom of drain needs repairing

indicators.note: something that needs repairing must be put back together, so the letters of drain are rearranged

explanation.surface: The base of a drain is broken and wants fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point, the depth of anything, is its bottom.

clue.text: Outlandish Government Department rule

parts.note: FO is the ... Office, a British government department
a monarch's rule is a reign

explanation.surface: A complaint about a bizarre regulation from a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: The FO, the Foreign Office, is the British ministry for overseas affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish means strange or alien, belonging to another country.

clue.text: Big retraction, in short, for a colonial city

definitions.text: Big retraction, in short, for a colonial city

parts.words: Big retraction, in short, for a colonial city
parts.note: the word Big turned round reads GIB, which is the everyday short name for the colony on the southern tip of Spain

explanation.walkthrough: Turning 'Big' back to front gives GIB, the familiar British shortening of the full name of this British territory and city at the mouth of the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rock is a British overseas territory and city, long a crown colony guarding the Strait.

clue.text: Saloon-keeper, not the American type

parts.note: in Britain a saloon is a car, so the place that keeps one is a shelter for a motor rather than a bar owner from a Western

explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is the British word for a sedan car; an American saloon-keeper would run a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where a car is kept or serviced houses a saloon car.

clue.text: Greek patriarch gets modern artists for magnificent church

parts.note: St Basil the Great was a Greek church father
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: A Greek church leader commissions contemporary artists for a grand cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA, the Institute of Contemporary Arts, is a London gallery for modern art.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand Roman-style church with special papal privileges, such as St Peter's, is a fine example of the type.

clue.text: Charges with assaults

definitions.meaning: to charge is to rush forward in an assault

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean violent offensives: rushing an enemy and striking someone are both such onslaughts.

clue.text: Teach to manage — that's just the ticket!

parts.note: to train is to teach
to fare is to get on or manage

explanation.surface: An approving remark about learning to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the ticket' sounds like approval, but it is a literal definition: the price of a rail ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: The cost of a rail journey is what one pays for a railway ticket.

clue.text: Wash out 24

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the other answer are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, straps for a horse

explanation.surface: A bare instruction to wash something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse something is to wash it lightly in clean water.

clue.text: Put down your weapons, but prepare for war

definitions.meaning: a drill command telling soldiers to lower rifles to rest butt on the ground
read literally, an instruction to command weapons to be got ready

explanation.surface: A contradictory pair of military instructions: disarm, yet ready yourself for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill order brings the rifle down beside the foot, while the phrase literally means requisition weaponry for fighting.

clue.text: Mark has a double holding

indicators.note: holding means the word for a double has the letter A placed inside it

parts.note: a double, an identical counterpart, is a twin

explanation.surface: Somebody called Mark keeps a lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is the first name of the American author Mark ___, pen name of Samuel Clemens.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Samuel Clemens, author of Tom Sawyer, began with Mark; the clue's first name stands for the surname.

clue.text: Permission for merger causing disregard of the law by Union?

indicators.note: by means set beside, so the word for union stands next to the word for lawlessness

parts.note: a union of two people is a wedding or matrimony
licence can mean excessive freedom, lawless disregard of rules

explanation.surface: A corporate merger approval that apparently lets a trade union flout the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merger' and 'Union' suggest business or labour, but the union is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding permit is the official authorisation two people need before they may be joined in matrimony.

clue.text: O'Hara put on old dressing gown

parts.note: Kim (Kimball O'Hara) is the boy hero of Kipling's novel Kim
clothes put on are on

explanation.surface: Someone named O'Hara wears an old robe.
explanation.walkthrough: O'Hara suggests Scarlett from Gone with the Wind; it is Kipling's Kim.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese wrap-over robe is widely worn in the West as a loose house robe.

clue.text: Girl needs a small sponge

definitions.meaning: a little shell-shaped French sponge cake

explanation.surface: A girl wants a little cake.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's name and the name of a small French shell-shaped cake.

clue.text: Runner on foot brings diamonds to Society girl

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An athlete brings a gift of diamonds to a debutante.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is the blade worn on the foot to glide over a rink.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot fitted with a steel blade glides like a sledge runner, attached to the wearer's foot.

clue.text: Modern hop flustered rounded person

indicators.note: flustered means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A modern dance step leaves a plump person flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a body type that is heavy and round, soft and plump.

clue.text: University has recording apparatus about same as a rain gauge

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same
a meter records quantities, like a gas meter

explanation.surface: A university owns a recording device that does much the same as a rain gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, short for ditto, means the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin udus, wet, the instrument measures rainfall, so it is a pluviometer.

clue.text: Scarlet woman's drink?

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
biddy is an informal word for a woman, especially an older one

explanation.surface: Asking what beverage a scarlet woman, a harlot, might favour.
explanation.walkthrough: RED BIDDY is a British slang name for cheap red wine mixed with methylated spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names a rough alcoholic mixture of cheap red wine and meths.

clue.text: Engraved dices in unusual shape

indicators.note: an unusual shape means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dice cut in an odd shape have been carved.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut into a surface, carved with a sharp tool.

clue.text: A football ground away from home

parts.note: a field is a pitch where football is played

explanation.surface: A football ground described as an away venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away from home' sounds like an away match; here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at a distance, out in the wider world rather than near one's dwelling.

clue.text: Equipment for healthy chaps beginning to tire

parts.note: fit means healthy
chaps are men

indicators.note: beginning to says take the first letter of tire

explanation.surface: Gear for healthy men who are starting to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitment is a fixed piece of furniture or apparatus, a fitting.

clue.text: Common sort of fish

definitions.meaning: freshwater fish other than salmon and trout are called this in Britain

explanation.surface: A common type of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: vulgar or crude, and British anglers' name for non-game freshwater fish like carp.

clue.text: A place of little ease till Flora Poste visited

definitions.text: A place of little ease till Flora Poste visited

parts.words: A place of little ease till Flora Poste visited
parts.note: Flora Poste is the heroine of Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic novel who tidies up her gloomy Sussex relatives' farm; little ease is cold consolation

explanation.walkthrough: The title of Stella Gibbons's novel combines a phrase for meagre consolation with a farm, which the heroine Flora Poste reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's Starkadder farmhouse is miserable until the heroine arrives to sort everyone out.

clue.text: West Indian getting round a woman

parts.note: C (circa) means about, approximately, as round does in round about
Eve was made from Adam's rib, so rib stands for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone from the West Indies gets around a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: RIB for woman comes from Genesis, where Eve is made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs were the native people of the Lesser Antilles, giving the Caribbean its name.

clue.text: The player to do nothing right

parts.note: to act is to do something
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The idle athlete who is right to do nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs a role on stage.

clue.text: Form of resin used for bridle straps

indicators.note: a form of a word is a version with its letters reshaped, so resin is rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree resin used to make horse tack.
explanation.definitionFit: The straps attached to a bit are what a rider holds to steer a horse.

clue.text: One who is a source of worry to a royal adviser

definitions.text: One who is a source of worry

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for royal, as in RN or RAF
a mentor is a trusted adviser

explanation.surface: Someone who troubles a counsellor to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who torments others, harassing them, causes them constant worry and distress.

clue.text: It shows the family line on money — it comes out of a trunk

definitions.text: it comes out of a trunk

indicators.note: in an across answer on means placed after, so the family line comes second, after the money

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a family tree shows a line of descent

explanation.surface: A genealogy chart printed on banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the family line after the money. A bread tree, such as the breadfruit, has fruit and branches growing out of its trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruiting tropical tree grows from a woody stem, its branches and crop springing from the trunk.

clue.text: Flambeau, the ex-malefactor Chesterton put inside

indicators.note: put inside says the letters sit within the words ex-malefactor Chesterton, straddling the join

explanation.surface: Flambeau is the reformed criminal whom G K Chesterton's stories once had jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Flambeau, the master thief turned detective in Chesterton's Father Brown stories, but 'put inside' signals letters lurking across 'malefactor Chesterton'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming brand carried to light the way, a burning hand-held light.
